title: Bridging Frustration and Non-Hermiticity via COMPASS: An Adaptive Biorthogonal Neural Quantum State Framework
authors: Lavoisier Wah, Flore K. Kunst, Mohamed Hibat-Allah
abstract: In this work, we introduce a complementary optimization method for progressive and adaptive state search (COMPASS) based on biorthogonal adaptive recurrent neural quantum states. Our approach combines an adaptive autoregressive architecture with a biorthogonal variational Monte Carlo scheme as well as a complementary optimization scheme that alternates between energy and variance minimization. This enables the stable convergence to ground-state eigenpairs, while avoiding Markov chain sampling through exact autoregressive generation. We demonstrate that for parity-time(PT)-symmetric Hamiltonians, unconstrained complex ansatze can spontaneously break PT symmetry during optimization, even in the unbroken phase, leading to spurious imaginary energies. Real-valued ansatze, on the other hand, naturally constrain the optimization to the correct physical manifold. Conversely, for generic non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonians without symmetry protection and complex spectra, complex ansatze are essential for capturing complex ground-state properties. Our results establish that physically-informed ansatz selection is crucial for reliable NH simulations. By combining adaptive architectures, biorthogonal optimization, and symmetry-aware modeling, this framework enables a direct study of 1D and 2D NH many-body systems without Hermitian embeddings or adiabatic continuation. Applying this framework to systems with frustrated magnetism, we show that gap frustration provides a quantitative shield against NH spectral instability, with the frustration gap setting a critical threshold for PT-symmetry breaking. Also, complexifying the frustration coupling itself generates a new topologically nontrivial network of diabolic level crossings, controlled by the phase of the complex coupling, that has no Hermitian analog. We term this novel spectral topology in NH frustrated systems the diabolic ring.
summary: The paper introduces COMPASS, an adaptive biorthogonal neural network framework designed for simulating Non-Hermitian many-body systems. It stabilizes ground state finding by combining energy and variance minimization into a progressive optimization scheme. This allows researchers to study exotic phenomena like spectral instability shielding via frustration and novel topological structures in NH quantum magnets.
main_problem: Developing a robust computational framework to study Non-Hermitian (NH) many-body systems, specifically bridging concepts of frustration and non-Hermiticity.
main_result: The proposed COMPASS framework successfully simulates NH systems directly, revealing that gap frustration shields against spectral instability and generating novel topological features like the diabolic ring.
method: It employs a Complementary Optimization Method for Progressive Adaptive State Search (COMPASS) using adaptive biorthogonal Neural Quantum States (NQSs). This method alternates between energy minimization and variance minimization to ensure stable convergence to ground-state eigenpairs.
model_or_system: The framework is applied to 1D and 2D NH many-body systems, including frustrated magnetism models based on extensions of the J1-J2 spin chain. The formalism requires a biorthogonal approach using left ($\Psi_L$) and right ($\Psi_R$) eigenstates.
key_observables: Ground-state eigenpairs ($E$), energy expectation value $\langle H angle$, energy variance ($\sigma^2$), and the fidelity of the biorthogonal overlap $|\langle\Psi_{L0}|\Psi_{R0}angle|$.
important_parameters: Frustration coupling strength, PT-symmetry breaking parameters (e.g., $\gamma/J_1$), system size ($N=1D$ up to 200, $N=2D$ up to 100).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that physically-informed ansatz selection is crucial for reliable NH simulations; it avoids Hermitian embeddings or adiabatic continuation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the COMPASS optimization process (adaptive growth, loss functions), PT-symmetry breaking in 1D Ising chains, and the emergence of Exceptional Points (EPs) when simulating frustrated NH models.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the COMPASS method using adaptive biorthogonal NQSs. It details the two-phase optimization process ($\mathcal{L}_e$ then $\mathcal{L}_v$) for finding ground states in NH systems. Finally, it applies this to frustrated magnetism to study spectral topology and EP emergence.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalizable numerical tool (COMPASS) that extends quantum simulation techniques beyond the Hermitian domain, allowing direct investigation of complex physics relevant to open or dissipative quantum systems.
